name: Soy
aliases: soy, soya, soybean, soya bean, soybeans, Glycine max, soy flour, soya flour, soy protein, soya protein, soy protein concentrate, soy protein isolate, textured soy protein, TVP, soja, harina de soja, proteína de soja, soja texturizada
what_is: Soy is a protein-rich legume. On a label it may appear as soy, soya, soy flour, soy protein, or soy protein concentrate or isolate. It is used to add protein and also to give body and structure to some foods.
why_botia: In several studies in women, a higher intake of soy was associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, and in survivors it was associated with lower mortality and recurrence. The association was clearer in populations that habitually eat more soy; other studies at moderate intakes did not find the same result. Isoflavone supplements did not show the same effects as soy foods.
can_1: Detect soy, soya, soy flour and the soy protein declarations when they are on the label.
can_2: Explain what the studies found and show the Woman information layer.
cannot_1: Determine how much soy a food contains, or how that compares with the intakes in the studies.
cannot_2: Determine how many isoflavones a soy ingredient carries, since the label does not say and it differs between whole soy foods and protein isolates.

sources.label: Meta-analysis: soy intake and breast cancer risk (2019)

title: Soy
description: Soy is a protein-rich legume that appears on labels as soy, soy flour or soy protein. In studies in women, higher soy intake was associated with lower breast cancer risk and, in survivors, with lower mortality and recurrence — though not in every population, and not with isoflavone supplements.
